holidays.name: National Mason Jar Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble glass jar. It holds pickles, preserves, overnight oats, fireflies, and the occasional fancy cocktail. Dust off your jars, put up some jam, or sip something cold from one.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of the patent John Landis Mason received on November 30, 1858, for his screw-threaded glass jar. The design made home canning safer and more reliable.
holidays.funFact: Mason's patent expired in the 1870s, so many other companies started making similar jars. That is why the word 'mason jar' became a generic name rather than one brand.

holidays.name: National Stay at Home Because You're Well Day
holidays.description: This holiday flips the usual sick day on its head. It encourages you to take a day off because you feel great, with no fever or sniffles required. Think of it as permission to enjoy a cozy day of pure leisure.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite among people who believe that wellness deserves a day off too.
holidays.funFact: It lands at the end of November, right before the December rush. That makes it a good moment for one last day of calm.

holidays.name: Computer Security Day
holidays.description: A day for tidying up your digital life. Change your passwords, update your software, back up your files, and think twice before clicking that suspicious link. It's like spring cleaning for your devices, only with more two-factor authentication.
holidays.origin: The Association for Computing Machinery started it in 1988. The aim was to raise awareness of computer security as personal computers and networks spread.
holidays.funFact: It began just after the 1988 Morris Worm, one of the first major internet worms. The worm slowed a large share of the then-tiny internet.
